summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational module capacity is 4.8 GW. Q1 sales were 334 MW against production of 408 MW. Management said the module market has become crowded.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (Odisha Phase 1)
segments.commentary: 2.4 GW cell capacity is under installation, with tool move-in done and a ramp of about 200 MW per month planned. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27 and says DCR cell orders have started for own cells.

segments.name: Non-module business (EPC, IPP, storage, B2C, transformers)
segments.commentary: Non-module revenue was 4-5% of total, with a target of 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1 and the transformer market is about INR 30,000 crore, targeted at INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 3.5-4 GW sales, revenue of about INR 6,000 crore, EBITDA margin of about 12%, PAT margin of 6-7%.
Management expects cell-led margin expansion in H2 FY27 and said cell EBITDA impact would be in the 'high double digits' (number not quantified).
ALMM-2 implementation was postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027 because of domestic cell shortages.
FY28 guidance to be discussed in Q3 FY27. Management called FY28 a 'milestone year' as utility DCR demand starts from April 2027.
Encapsulant capacity to rise from 2 GW to 5 GW; the announcement on equipment is expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha Phase 1 (57 acres): 2.4 GW cell and 4 GW module. About INR 1,000 crore of capex incurred so far; Phase 1 total is about INR 1,850 crore.
Phase 2 (27 acres): 3.6 GW cell, taking total cell capacity to 6 GW. Site work to start by end-Q2 FY27, completion by end-FY28, capex about INR 1,600-1,700 crore.
Phase 3: 6 GW ingot and wafer, targeted for FY29 and aligned with ALMM-3. Planning has started.
Total capex across the programme is roughly INR 3,500 crore. Peak net debt is expected at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.
Cell line ramp-up expected by end-August or early September 2026, with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026.
demand_pricing: Confirmed order book of about 6.35 GW (about 132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore per management, with execution over 12-18 months.
Mix: about 70% utility and 30% C&I/open access. About 30% of orders are DCR. Retail is excluded from the book and runs at about 20% of monthly sales.
Pricing: about 30% of C&I orders are fixed-price. In utility, about 30-40% are variable-price (cost pass-through) and the rest fixed-price.
New orders: INR 138 crore module order in July 2026 (execution by December 2026) and about INR 400 crore accepted by a subsidiary on 11 August 2026 (execution by March 2027).
DCR cell margins are quoted at 18-20%. Management said spot cell-purchase orders are not in the order book.
Customers deferred purchases amid the Iran war, cost volatility and ALMM-1 vs ALMM-2 uncertainty. Management said demand was weak in May-June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. It also said it declined to execute orders where input costs could not be passed on. Q1 margin of 8.33% was better than Q4 FY26's 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected by end-August or early September 2026, with 200 MW per month from the 2.4 GW line. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27. Full ramp-up is expected in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR 1,250 crore. Capex incurred is about INR 1,000 crore out of a roughly INR 3,500 crore programme. Net debt is expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers until Q3 FY27. It said large utility projects tendered from December 2025 (18-24 month cycles) will drive DCR demand from April 2027, making FY28 a milestone year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-module business is 4-5% of revenue, targeted at 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1. Management targets 8-10% of a transformer market of about INR 30,000 crore (INR 55,000 crore by 2031) and INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.
